title: Table-driven tests: the standard Go idiom

videos.script: Lesson 25 ended with five subtests that differed only in their data. This lesson writes the data once, as a table. {{table}} Each row is a case: a name, an input, the answer you expect. One loop turns every row into a subtest. A new case becomes one more line. {{names}} Then the names. A row's name is what the report prints when it fails, so it should say what makes the case different. You run one row by its name, and you anchor the pattern so it does not catch a neighbour. {{top}} Last, a second function, the most frequent words, and a test that passes on one run and fails on the next. The message it prints says exactly what went wrong, and the cause is a map walked in random order. {{fix}} You fix it, and run the test a hundred times to be sure. {{close}} Lesson 27 tests code that depends on something you would rather not call.
